newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices regain on reduced inflows.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices regain on reduced inflows.

text.p: Indian cotton prices bounced back from reduced level on Tuesday as inflows fell since farmers preferred to hold onto new crops, traders said.
Fresh buying by the state-owned Cotton Corporation of India at producing centres also helped the recovery.

Bengal-deshi ready delivery spot rates rose by 40/70 to 910/960 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while November delivery was quoted at 960/975. Long-staple Gujarat Sankar-4 rose by 300/500 to 20,500/21,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). "Farmers preferred to bring limited quantities of new crop cotton in the market due to poor prices," one broker said.
